layer2_mcp_http.description: Real MCP initialize, tools/list and tools/call requests over the sidecar HTTP /mcp endpoint, connected to the live ZBrush bridge.
layer2_mcp_http.finding: Real MCP tools/call succeeded only for affinity:any catalog and dialog tools; 3 of 7 calls succeeded. ZBrush scene tools declare affinity: main. Core is not the defect: with no host dispatcher attached (host_dispatcher_attached=False) its Rust dispatcher correctly refuses declared main-affinity actions rather than running them off the host main thread. The missing wiring is in the adapter, which registers only an in-process executor and runs a sleeping sidecar main loop with no main-thread pump. The same tools do real work through the socket-bridge JSON-RPC path (Layer 1), which does not establish that MCP HTTP can complete ZBrush scene work. The full MCP capability-demonstration acceptance is therefore not closed.
layer2_mcp_http.root_cause: The adapter, not Core, is where the wiring is missing. In sidecar mode dcc-mcp-zbrush _executor.py calls only register_inprocess_executor() and attaches no host QueueDispatcher/BlockingDispatcher, while cli.py's sidecar main loop only sleeps and pumps no main-thread work. Core behaves as designed: sidecar_skill_server.py attach_dispatcher is a no-op and inprocess_executor.py resolve_host_dispatcher() returns None (host_dispatcher_attached=False), so the Rust dispatcher returns THREAD_AFFINITY_UNAVAILABLE for declared thread_affinity=main actions and only affinity:any tools execute. This is an unfixed adapter-side defect; this entry makes no Core change and claims no fix.

successful_calls.return_kind: real skill catalog from the running sidecar

tools.description: Click one labelled button (for example OK, Cancel, Yes, No) on the modal ZBrush note that blocks ZBrush, then verify that the bridge answers again. Reads the window first, matches exactly one visible label, posts one mouse click at its centre, and returns dismissed=true only when ZBrush is free. Refuses when no dialog blocks ZBrush unless force=true.

allow_destructive.description: Confirm a destructive note (delete, overwrite, discard, undo). Set only after the user approved; Cancel never needs it.

button_name.description: Button label exactly as returned in button_candidates by get_active_dialog.

force.description: Click even when the bridge answers (a non-blocking note).

match.description: How button_name is compared with the visible labels (case-insensitive).

output_dir.description: Optional existing directory for the PNG screenshot taken before the click.

probe_timeout_secs.description: Seconds to wait for each bridge ping.

process_id.description: Optional ZBrush process id when several ZBrush processes run.

tools.name: zbrush_dialog__click_dialog_button

tools.description: Detect whether a modal ZBrush note or popup dialog is blocking ZBrush, and read it. Probes the socket bridge from the sidecar with a short timeout (it never queues work on the ZBrush main thread); when the status is blocked, captures the ZBrush window (ZBrush draws its notes inside it) or a message box window, and returns the OCR dialog_text, the clickable button_candidates, dialog_kind (informational, question, destructive_confirmation), and the screenshot path.

force_capture.description: Capture and read the window even when ZBrush answers the bridge, for example to read a non-blocking note.

output_dir.description: Optional existing directory for the PNG screenshot (default is the system temp directory).

probe_timeout_secs.description: Seconds to wait for the bridge ping before ZBrush counts as blocked.

process_id.description: Optional ZBrush process id when several ZBrush processes run.

tools.name: zbrush_dialog__get_active_dialog

return.message: No modal dialog is blocking ZBrush
